title: The Rivergate of Patagonia's dry side
premise: Noor Thornbury, a riverboat captain haunted by a promise made to a drowned friend, is hired to ferry a government survey team up the Rio Seco on Patagonia's arid eastern slope. When the team vanishes from a moored camp, Noor and the team's cartographer, Elena Vasquez, discover the men were silenced by the concession company whose permits expire in forty days — and that the river's forbidden source hides water rights worth fortunes. Racing the permit clock and the company's enforcers upstream through gorges and ghost towns, Noor must choose between delivering Elena to safety and honoring the memory of everyone the river has taken. At the source, they expose the company's forged surveys, but Noor pays with the boat — and finally stops moving.
about_author: August Galloway is the pen name of a former merchant-marine officer who spent six years running cargo on South American rivers before turning to writing. They live in a coastal town in Wales, where they still cannot sleep without the sound of water.

chapters.title: The Mood of Sandbars
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. A dawn run down the lower Rio Seco establishes Noor's intimate knowledge of the river and restless refusal to stay anywhere longer than a week. A telegram arrives offering triple pay for a government charter. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as freedom.

chapters.title: Triple Pay
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. In the port town of Puerto Árido, Noor meets the survey team: five men led by the brittle, secretive Mr. Calloway-Hurst, plus cartographer Elena Vasquez, who sees through Noor's deflections immediately. Noor signs anyway — the money means never stopping again. Beat: greed wrestling with instinct.

chapters.title: Cargo That Breathes
chapters.summary: Elena's POV. Loading day; Elena notices crates marked for drilling equipment no survey needs, and quietly photographs the manifests. She and Noor circle each other with wary professional respect. Beat: first crack in both their armor.

chapters.title: Upstream of Maps
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. The journey begins past the last charted reach. Sandbars shift overnight; the crew works the winches. Calloway-Hurst burns a page of his own notebook. Beat: the river turning strange, tension rising like pressure.

chapters.title: The Town That Sold Its Water
chapters.summary: Elena's POV. A stop at Estancia Salada, a dying sheep town whose wells went dry after the concession company arrived. An old woman gives Elena a hand-drawn map of the upper gorge and warns: 'The river remembers who drinks first.' Beat: dread taking root.

chapters.title: Night Anchorage
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Moored below the gorge, Noor tells Elena about Tomás, the friend who drowned saving Noor's boat — and the promise to keep moving so the guilt can't catch up. Elena admits she took this job to escape a marriage arranged by her family's duty. Beat: love beginning against both their wills.

chapters.title: Empty Tents
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Dawn: four of the five surveyors are gone from camp — gear intact, coffee cold, no tracks in the dust. Only Calloway-Hurst remains, too calm. Elena finds boot prints ending mid-slope, as if lifted. Beat: fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: What the Manifests Said
chapters.summary: Elena's POV. Elena shows Noor her photographs: the 'survey' was a cover for staking water claims at the source before rival concessions expire. Calloway-Hurst confesses he was ordered to let it happen. Beat: betrayal reframing everything.

chapters.title: The Company Boat
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. A black-hulled launch appears downstream — the concession company's enforcers, led by the courteous, terrifying Inspector Reyes. Noor runs the boat through a night passage no sane pilot would attempt. Beat: Noor's skill as survival, adrenaline and awe.

chapters.title: Gorge of Whistling Stones
chapters.summary: Elena's POV. The rapids of the upper gorge nearly capsize them; a deckhand, Bruno, is lost overboard and saved by seconds. Elena realizes she is no longer documenting — she is committed. Beat: courage discovered under terror.

chapters.title: Ghost Town, Living Radio
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. In abandoned mining town Cobre Muerto they find the missing surveyors' belongings and a working radio relaying Reyes's orders: bring back the woman and the maps, sink the rest. Calloway-Hurst disappears in the night. Beat: isolation closing like a trap.

chapters.title: Two Against the Current
chapters.summary: Elena's POV. With two crew paid off and gone, only Noor, Elena, and young deckhand Pilar remain. Elena chooses to keep going upstream rather than take the road out — choosing Noor over the safe life waiting for her. Beat: love declared through decision, not words.

chapters.title: The Permit Clock
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Eleven days left on the concession. Reyes catches them at a lock and offers Noor a bribe and amnesty; Noor refuses, and Reyes lets them go — a message that the real trap waits above. Beat: power showing its patience.

chapters.title: Salt in the Engine
chapters.summary: Pilar's POV. The engine fails in dead water; Pilar, the youngest voice, holds the narrative as they drift, repair, and nearly starve. Elena teaches Pilar to read the current charts. Beat: found family forming in extremity.

chapters.title: Calloway-Hurst Returns
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. The broken surveyor staggers into their camp, having walked out of the high country — he saw the source, and what the company built there: a dam and diversion tunnel already stealing the headwaters. He dies of exposure after giving them his field book. Beat: grief hardening into purpose.

chapters.title: The Forbidden Reach
chapters.summary: Elena's POV. Past the posted boundary, through fog and standing water, they enter the reach no chart admits exists. Elena maps it as they go — an act of witness. Beat: awe and transgression intertwined.

chapters.title: Source
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. They find the spring-fed lake behind the illegal dam, and the vanished surveyors — alive, imprisoned as witnesses. Reyes waits with rifles. He offers Elena partnership in the new concession. Beat: corruption making its final, seductive offer.

chapters.title: Water Remembers Who Drinks First
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Climax: Noor scuttles the company launch in the spillway while Elena broadcasts the true survey and the old woman's map over Reyes's own radio to every station on the river. Reyes, exposed, tries to flood the evidence; the dam groans. Beat: sacrifice meeting cunning.

chapters.title: The Breaking of the Dam
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. The dam fails; the released headwater floods the diversion works and carries away the forged records. Noor goes back for Pilar and is caught in the surge — surviving by surrendering the boat, Tomás's boat, to the river at last. Beat: the debt to memory finally paid.

chapters.title: Downstream
chapters.summary: Elena's POV. The survivors ride the flood's aftermath downriver; the surveyors testify, the concession collapses, and the estancias' wells begin to rise. Elena publishes the true map under her own name. Beat: justice arriving quiet and imperfect.

chapters.title: Where Noor Stopped
chapters.summary: Noor's POV. Months later, Noor pilots a small ferry at Estancia Salada — a fixed route, a fixed home. Elena stays through winter, then chooses to stay altogether. Noor learns that stopping costs something, and pays it gladly. Beat: peace earned, not given.

chapters.title: The Rivergate
chapters.summary: Pilar's POV, years later. Pilar, now a captain herself, passes the rebuilt spring and the stone marker Elena placed naming the lost. The river runs full to the sea. Final beat: memory kept alive by those who carry it forward.
